data.why: The repository ships its own precomputed results (results/2505_1.0.0/afterglow.csv, flares.csv, pulses.csv, and per-burst BAT/XRT fit figures) that app.py and the pages load directly; there is no upload workflow, so nothing needs to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Look up a specific Swift GRB by name and inspect its fitted XRT and BAT light curves with overlaid afterglow, flare, and pulse model components
Read off a burst's fitted model parameters and derived temporal/energetic quantities (e.g. break times, peak luminosity, fluence) from the summary table
Explore population-level scatter plots of afterglow parameters against each other, toggling log/linear axes and a third color-coded parameter
Explore the combined flare and pulse population, filtering which set is shown and coloring by parameter or by specific GRB
Highlight one or more named GRBs across a population plot to see where they fall relative to the rest of the sample
Click an outlying or interesting point in a population plot to jump directly to that burst's detail view in the Burst Viewer

review.summary: The tree matches the README closely: look up a Swift GRB and inspect its XRT/BAT fits and parameter tables, then explore the afterglow and flare/pulse populations with highlighting and click-through, with well-chosen features, all replayed and backed by screens. Before filing, it needs a few accuracy fixes: f3's carry-over and greying claim, noting that the fit plots are static images, and one weak evidence cite.
